headline: Day-Entry and River Trip Permits for the Dehcho Wilderness
reservation: All visitors entering the park, whether for a day trip to Virginia Falls or an extended river expedition, must obtain a permit from Parks Canada. Overnight river trips often require an application months in advance due to strict daily launch limits, while flight-seeing visitors must ensure their tour operator has a valid business license. Confirm all current reservation requirements and river quotas through the Fort Simpson park office.

days.title: The Thunder of Ná́įicho (Virginia Falls)
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Fort Simpson via floatplane

stops.name: Virginia Falls (Ná́įicho)
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalks to witness the South Nahanni River drop 96 meters around the massive Mason's Rock.

stops.name: Sluice Box
stops.detail: Observe the powerful whitewater rapids immediately above the falls from the designated viewing platforms.

days.driving: Allow 1–1.5 hours for air charter; conditions vary
days.note: Boardwalks may be slippery from mist; maintain a steady pace to catch your scheduled return flight.

days.title: Canyons and Karst Formations
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from a riverside camp in the Second Canyon

stops.name: The Gate and Pulpit Rock
stops.detail: Navigate the narrowest section of the river where the water carves through vertical limestone walls.

stops.name: Grotto Creek
stops.detail: Hike into the side canyons to see unique karst features and hidden spring-fed pools.

days.driving: Local river travel or walking; conditions vary
days.note: River travel speeds depend heavily on current flow and water levels in the canyons.

days.title: Thermal Springs and Prairie Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Deadmen Valley area

stops.name: Kraus Hotsprings
stops.detail: Visit the site of an old homestead where geothermal waters meet the river's edge.

stops.name: The Splits
stops.detail: Watch the river widen into a labyrinth of gravel bars and islands as it approaches the park boundary.

days.note: Stay alert for shifting gravel bars that can ground rafts or canoes in late summer.

intel.title: Gateway Staging
intel.text: Vehicle parking is centralized at floatplane bases in Fort Simpson or Nahanni Butte. There are no road-accessible parking areas within the park reserve itself.

intel.title: Radio Communication
intel.text: Expect zero cellular service throughout the park. Many river travelers carry VHF radios or satellite messengers to communicate with park staff and air charters.

intel.title: Fort Simpson Hub
intel.text: This is the last reliable location to source fuel and groceries before heading into the backcountry. Remote communities like Nahanni Butte have extremely limited commercial services.

intel.title: Peak Flow Window
intel.text: Most travelers visit between late June and August. Early season may face high water hazards, while late August can bring colder temperatures and shorter days.

intel.title: Fly-In Only
intel.text: Access is primarily via floatplane from Fort Simpson or Watson Lake. While the South Nahanni River is the main thoroughfare, it is a technical wilderness river with no road access.

plan.arrival: Arrive in Fort Simpson via Highway 1 or regional flight, visit the Parks Canada Visitor Centre for mandatory orientation, and finalize gear with your outfitter.
plan.vehicle: A 4WD vehicle is recommended for the long gravel haul on the Liard and Mackenzie Highways to reach the gateway towns, but cannot enter the park.
plan.goldenHour: Sunlight hitting the canyon walls at The Gate, typically during mid-summer evening hours.
